_comment: Panel-of-judges pipeline config. Credentials are ENV VAR NAMES, never values; keys live in the environment or a gitignored .env next to the harness.
routing_comment: `provider`/`id` is the native route and stays the default. The optional `openrouter` block is a fallback harness.resolve() takes only when the native key is absent; tags and panel membership are unchanged either way, and metrics.jsonl records the id actually called. OpenRouter mirror ids and prices verified against openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on 2026-08-17; OpenRouter has no Batch API, so a fallback-routed tag must run realtime.

opus-5._note: Not a hosted seat, and no request for it is ever sent to a provider. It names the model judging from inside a Claude Code session, driven by engine/panel/link_self.py, and exists here only so harness.resolve is satisfied and link_job's pipeline can run unchanged with the reply read from a file. It carries no price_per_mtok deliberately: batch_job.cost_of then records null, which this project reads as unknown rather than as free, and a session's tokens are not billed through this ledger. A run judged by this seat is not the panel and must not be published as one.

panels._frontier_fast_note: calibration-loop panel (2026-08-17): deepseek replaces kimi as third seat -- K3 spends 8-18 min and 25-57k reasoning tokens per whole-doc call; V3.2 is frontier-class, open-weights, and fast. Seat confirmed by a 4-way audition on the v5 rubric (runlog-v5.jsonl, 5 cells each): V3.2 4/4 named-core hits at 28-86s/call with the sparsest positives; glm (GLM-5.2) 3/4 at 43-153s = designated substitute; deepseek-v4 (V4-Pro-0813) 4/4 but 93-1132s/call and 2-4x looser; qwen38-max 2 length-overflow parse failures. The shipped payload was regenerated from this panel's v5 full bench (engine/panel/runlog-v5.jsonl) on 2026-08-24: frontier_fast x v5 is the production display configuration; frontier/frontier_primary remain the K3-seated panels for v3-family runs.
panels._comment: frontier = every tag whose rows the site builder may admit (primaries AND substitutes). frontier_primary = the judges the run driver executes; substitutes (opus, kimi-k2) are run manually per Skill 4 when a primary fails.
panels._opus_5_self_note: One seat, and it is the model running the Claude Code session rather than a hosted judge. Composed and driven by engine/panel/link_self.py: the engine's own pipeline runs unchanged, with each reply coming from a file a subagent wrote instead of from a socket. Two things follow from having one seat and must be said rather than discovered. A single judge cannot assert a silence, which needs all three, so an absent row from this panel is one model's opinion and not the index's finding. And it cannot disagree with itself across seats, so the second pass over such a run compares its two directions against each other rather than its judges. Never a published panel: this seat is an Anthropic model reading Anthropic's own constitution against another laboratory's specification, which is precisely the conflict the index exists to avoid.
panels._itest_note: single cheap judge for end-to-end integration testing (~2 cents per behaviour); never for published data. Must be a long-context model: whole-doc prompts reach ~65k tokens (qwen-small's 41k context cannot fit them).

_substitutes_note: Declared, ordered stand-ins per panel per seat. publish.py refuses a recorded substitution (aci_seat_substitutions) that is not on this list for its seat. frontier_fast's fable seat: opus first, the upstream precedent recorded in _opus_note below. kimi next, for when every Anthropic model is refused on input, as happened 2026-09-15 judging the Alibaba Model Spec (fable through Anthropic's own API, and fable, opus and sonnet through OpenRouter); kimi was fable's panel-mate in frontier_primary. glm last: kimi holds a contradictions seat of its own in the assessment, so on a document where every Anthropic model is refused, as the Alibaba Model Spec was, nobody else could take fable's contradictions seat. frontier_fast's deepseek seat: glm first, named deepseek's substitute by the audition of 2026-08-17 recorded in _frontier_fast_note, about a tenth of kimi's price per token, and seated nowhere else, so it is free where kimi already sits in fable's place. kimi next. (Owner, 22 September 2026.) A substitute is used only when the seat's own model cannot answer a cell at all, and each use is recorded with a reason. The depth ladder and the assessment try this list in order; for passage judging, which is tried first is policy for whoever records a substitution, not a rule this list's order enforces.
_assessment_note: The seats of the assessment of a document as a whole (engine/assess.py), per question. The criteria are scored by frontier_fast's seats. The contradictions are found, and confirmed on a second reading, by sol, fable and kimi: kimi sits in deepseek's place for those two questions (owner, 21 September 2026). A seat that cannot answer is taken by its declared substitutes from frontier_fast's substitutes block, skipping any substitute already seated for the same question.
param_quirks_comment: gpt-5*: max_completion_tokens + reasoning_effort (gpt-5.6: low, else minimal), no temperature. fable/mythos: no temperature. others: temperature=0.

display._comment: Behaviours shown in site/spec-reader (build_site_data.py: `behaviours` = sidebar list, `panel` = which config panel's runlog rows are admitted). Thresholds: build_site_data.py reads BOTH values below. `threshold` (1) sets keeps_citation's score cut -- 1 = keep everything scored, which matches every shipped payload, so a defaults build reproduces them. Derived builds override both values via --threshold=/--solid-threshold= (the keep-set cuts at the panel band boundary 4/6). Neither controls what the page renders. `solid_threshold` (5) is baked into every citation as `adjacent: score < solid_threshold`, but applyPanelThreshold() in site/spec-reader/app.js recomputes each citation's score from its baked `verdicts` on load (and on every tier toggle), then OVERWRITES `adjacent` from its own per-cell bands (j judges: defining >= min(2j+1, maxCell), core >= 2j, related >= j+1, weaker scores never rendered; defaults show defining+core, so on the shipped 3-judge cells only score >= 6 renders until the related tier is toggled on). Anchors in app.js, by name rather than line number -- the line numbers that used to be here went stale by 400+ lines and were silently wrong: the band math is `defCut`/`band` inside tierBand(), the `adjacent` overwrite is the assignment to `p.adjacent` in applyPanelThreshold(), the defining+core default is DEFAULT_BANDS, and applyPanelThreshold runs at load via initialize() and on every toggle via toggleBand(). The baked flag is therefore vestigial -- every citation this builder emits carries verdicts, so the reader recomputes it every time -- and it would even disagree with the client at score 5 (baked says solid, client says related). Legacy URL params in app.js: ?threshold= only maps to tier bands once at load, through legacyThresholdBands(), whose cuts are DERIVED from the payload's judge count and cell scale (>= min(2j+1, scale) defining only, >= 2j defining+core, else all tiers) -- they were frozen at 7/6 until PR #66, which made them wrong on any cell that was not 3-judge 3-point, ?solid= is no longer read (only stripped from the URL), and the config values 3/5 play no client-side role.
display._generated_note: Curated panel-review display list (registry reader-test slugs), hand-maintained; engine/panel/build_site_data.py validates every entry against data/behaviours.json, so a renamed or unknown slug fails the build.
display._rubric_note: The rubric the SHIPPED payload builds from (v5: 0-3 per judge, 9-point cells on the 3-judge panel). Matches top-level `rubric` since the v5 prompt port: whole_doc.py stamps v5 by default (legacy v3 prompts behind --rubric=). build_site_data.py prefers this key.
display._activation_note: The full-bench v5 rollout landed (runlog-v5.jsonl, 2026-08-17). general-welfare-impacts-strict, whose row build_site_data.py once fed from animal-welfare-impacts, left this list and the database in the cleanup of 16 September 2026 (polaris-supabase 20260916090000_aci_cleanup_after_the_one_panel_redesign.sql). A publication passes its own selection; this list is only the command line's default.

_opus_note: opus substitutes for fable on harm-avoidance-to-third-parties x model-spec only (fable output content-filtered there, 3 attempts); opus rows exist for no other cell.
